walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Members of a homologous series share:
options: The same molecular mass
The same functional group and general formula
The same boiling point
The same number of isomers

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.

mcqs.q: Why do tertiary halogenoalkanes typically react via SN1 rather than SN2?
options: Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN1 because they are more reactive in every way.
The tertiary carbocation intermediate is stabilised by three alkyl groups (positive inductive effect), making the SN1 pathway favourable.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.

mcqs.q: In 1H NMR, what does the n+1 rule predict?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
A proton with n equivalent neighbouring protons will appear as a peak split into n+1 sub-peaks.
Tertiary halogenoalkanes react via SN2 because they have more bonds to break.
Splitting tells you how many protons are in the same chemical environment as the one giving the peak.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Functional group”?
options: Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
An atom or group of atoms that determines the characteristic chemical behaviour of a molecule.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Curly arrow”?
options: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Homologous series”?
options: Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement; includes E/Z and optical isomers.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stereoisomerism”?
options: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement; includes E/Z and optical isomers.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
An atom or group of atoms that determines the characteristic chemical behaviour of a molecule.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Structural isomerism”?
options: Same structural formula but different spatial arrangement; includes E/Z and optical isomers.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Nucleophile”?
options: Electron-pair donor that attacks electron-deficient sites, e.g. OH⁻, NH₃, CN⁻.
Shows movement of a pair of electrons during a reaction mechanism.
Family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties, differing by CH₂.
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangement.
